question: What does 'class' mean in Python?
answer: 'class' in Python means a blueprint for creating objects [S1] [S2]. Objects are instances of classes, and classes define how objects are initialized and what methods they can have [S1].

citations.title: Python Lecture Notes
citations.text: 6. Object-Oriented Programming A class is a blueprint and an object is an instance of that class. The special method __init__ initializes a new object, and self is the conventional name for the instance. Attributes store data; methods are functions defined inside the class. class Account:  def __init__(self, owner, balance=0):  self.owner = owner  self.balance = balance  def deposit(self, amount):  self.balance += amount Inheritance lets a subclass reuse a parent class: class Savings(Account). The subclass can override methods and call the parent version through super(). Polymorphism means different classes can provide the same method name, so code can call obj.describe() without knowing the exact class. Encapsulation is the idea of keeping internal state controlled. citations.title: Python Glossary Overloaded Terms
citations.text: class: in Python a class is a blueprint for creating objects. It is not a category label as in classification problems. function: a reusable block of code defined with def. It is not necessarily a mathematical function. mode: when opening a file the mode string such as "r", "w" or "a" says how the file is used. statistics.mode(data) is a different thing: it returns the most frequent value. sample: random.sample(population, k) draws k unique elements without replacement. It has nothing to do with a statistical sample unless you use it to build one. normal: random.gauss(mu, sigma) and random.normalvariate(mu, sigma) draw numbers from a normal distribution. seed: random.seed(n) makes the random sequence reproducible, so a program prints the same random numbers on every run. iterable: an object you can loop over, such as a list or string.
